english.note: This is the all-purpose noun for danger, including both risk of harm and a hazardous source or situation.
Use this as the all-purpose noun for danger or a situation in which someone may be harmed.
Use this when “menace” emphasizes the danger or hazardous nature of the situation rather than a threatening force.
Use this for an imminent or concrete danger rather than an abstract assessment of probability.

examples.english: That area still hasn't been closed off; there's danger in going in.
examples.traditional: 嗰度仲未封路，入去有危險㗎。
